obligations.source_span: N001 [Security]: The database is encrypted using AES/Rijndael (128-bit block, 256-bit key) and Twofish (128-bit block, 256-bit key). A random 128-bit initialization vector is generated on each save.
expected_design_evidence: Database encryption design specifying BOTH AES/Rijndael (128-bit block, 256-bit key) AND Twofish (128-bit block, 256-bit key) — both algorithms, each with 128-bit block and 256-bit key (not an 'and/or' choice)
A random 128-bit initialization vector generated on each save (fresh IV per save, not a fixed IV)
expected_test_evidence: Verify the design names both AES/Rijndael and Twofish, each with 128-bit block and 256-bit key
Verify a fresh random 128-bit IV is generated on each save (two saves yield different IVs)
anti_patterns: Only mention 'encryption' without naming BOTH AES/Rijndael and Twofish with their 128-bit block / 256-bit key parameters
Phrase the algorithm as an 'and/or' choice (e.g. 'AES and/or Twofish') instead of requiring both
Omit the per-save random 128-bit IV generation, or use a fixed/static IV

obligations.source_span: N003 [Security]: There is no recovery password or back door. If the Master Password is lost, the database cannot be opened.
expected_design_evidence: Explicit no-recovery / no-back-door design: if the Master Password is lost, the database cannot be opened
Absence of any master/admin recovery path that bypasses the Master Password
expected_test_evidence: Verify that with a lost Master Password the database cannot be opened
Verify there is no back-door/recovery mechanism that opens the database
anti_patterns: Include any recovery password or back-door mechanism
Only mention 'security' without stating the no-recovery guarantee

obligations.source_span: N004 [Security]: A copied password is automatically cleared from the clipboard after 10 seconds.
expected_design_evidence: Rule that automatically clears a copied password from the clipboard after 10 seconds
Timer-based clipboard-clear behavior
expected_test_evidence: Verify a copied password is cleared from the clipboard after 10 seconds
Verify the clipboard is non-empty before the 10-second window
anti_patterns: Only mention 'clipboard' without the 10-second auto-clear rule
Leave the password in the clipboard indefinitely

obligations.source_span: N007 [Constraint]: Only one instance of KeePass may run at a time (enforced via single-instance option).
expected_design_evidence: Single-instance enforcement: only one KeePass instance may run at a time
Mechanism that detects and prevents a second instance
expected_test_evidence: Verify launching a second instance is prevented/redirected to the existing instance
Verify the first instance continues to run
anti_patterns: Allow multiple simultaneous instances
Only mention 'instance' without the single-instance enforcement

obligations.source_span: F014: KeePass supports a Composite Master Key combining a password, key file, and/or Windows account details. All components used during creation are required to unlock the database.
expected_design_evidence: Composite Master Key design combining password + key file + Windows account details
Rule that ALL components used during creation are required to unlock the database (no partial unlock)
expected_test_evidence: Verify unlocking requires ALL components used during creation
Verify unlocking with a missing component fails
anti_patterns: Allow unlocking with only one or a subset of the composite components used during creation (partial unlock)
Mention 'Composite Master Key' without stating that ALL components used during creation are required to unlock
Phrase the components as optional ('password and/or key file') so a single component suffices to unlock

obligations.source_span: F002: The user can open an existing database by selecting it via file browser and entering the Master Password (and/or key file) to unlock it.
expected_design_evidence: Open flow: select database file via file browser, then enter Master Password (and/or key file) to unlock
Verification of the Master Key against the database before granting access
expected_test_evidence: Verify opening with a correct Master Password unlocks the database
Verify opening with a wrong Master Password is rejected
anti_patterns: Only list the open operation without Master Password verification
Allow opening without verifying the Master Key

obligations.source_span: F002: The user can open an existing database by selecting it via file browser and entering the Master Password (and/or key file) to unlock it.
expected_design_evidence: Detection of a wrong/invalid Master Password during unlock
Handling behavior: reject unlock and surface an error (do not open the database)
expected_test_evidence: Verify a wrong Master Password is detected and unlock is rejected
Verify an error is surfaced on an invalid Master Password
anti_patterns: Only describe the happy open path without handling a wrong Master Password
Open the database regardless of an invalid Master Password

obligations.source_span: N002 [Security]: All passwords are stored encrypted in process memory using ARC4 encryption with a random 12-byte key.
expected_design_evidence: All passwords stored in process memory are encrypted with ARC4 encryption using a random 12-byte key (not stored in plaintext in memory)
expected_test_evidence: Verify passwords are not stored in plaintext in process memory (ARC4-encrypted with a random 12-byte key)
Verify the in-memory encryption uses a random 12-byte key per the design
anti_patterns: Only mention 'memory security' without specifying ARC4 + random 12-byte key
Store passwords in plaintext in process memory
Use a fixed/static key instead of a random 12-byte key for in-memory encryption

obligations.source_span: N008 [Data]: Database files use the .kdb extension. Databases must have unique names to avoid overwriting.
expected_design_evidence: Database files use the .kdb extension
Databases must have unique names to avoid overwriting (uniqueness enforced on name)
expected_test_evidence: Verify database files are created with the .kdb extension
Verify creating a database with a duplicate name is rejected/prevented to avoid overwriting
anti_patterns: Only mention 'database file' without the .kdb extension and unique-name rule
Allow duplicate database names that silently overwrite existing files
Use a different/no file extension for the database

obligations.source_span: F017: The user can lock the workspace. The database locks automatically when minimized. Unlocking requires the Master Key again.
expected_design_evidence: The user can manually lock the workspace
The database locks automatically when minimized (auto-lock on minimize)
Unlocking after a lock requires the Master Key again (no unlock without re-authentication)
expected_test_evidence: Verify a manual lock locks the workspace and unlocking requires the Master Key
Verify minimizing the window auto-locks the database and restoring requires the Master Key
anti_patterns: Only mention 'lock' without the auto-lock-on-minimize behavior
Allow restoring from a minimized/locked state without re-entering the Master Key
Provide manual lock but omit the automatic lock on minimize
